caption: Investment Funds
vo: A fund subscription touches the client, the fund manager, Operations and the transfer agent. Let's follow one, end to end, with every control in place.

caption: Sign in as Vanessa Ah-Kee — Fund Manager
vo: Meet Vanessa Ah-Kee, our fund manager. She captures and follows client fund orders.

caption: Funds: the Genesis Global Funds range
vo: Here's the Genesis Global Funds range. Asset class, horizon, how much our clients hold, and the share classes.

caption: Share classes: what the client actually buys
vo: But clients don't buy a fund, they buy a share class. Each has its currency, a risk rating, a minimum, and the latest NAV.

caption: Each share class holds the dealing rules
vo: And the dealing rules live here too. The ISIN, entry and exit fees, how often it deals, and the cut-off time.

caption: NAV History: one price per share class per dealing date
vo: Prices come in from the transfer agent, one per share class per dealing date. Holdings are always valued at the latest NAV.

caption: Fund Orders ▸ Fund subscription opens a three-step wizard
vo: Now let's take an order. Investor and fund, then amount and payment, then suitability.

caption: First, a client whose KYC is still in progress
vo: We'll start with a tricky one. Amit Lebrasse's KYC is still in progress. What happens if Vanessa tries to take Amit's order anyway?

caption: The amount is in the share class currency — here US dollars
vo: Sixty thousand, in the share class currency, US dollars. The Fixed Maturity Bond 2029 has a minimum of fifty thousand US dollars.

caption: Payment not received yet, so "Payment proof received" stays unticked
vo: The money hasn't arrived yet, so payment proof stays unticked. We'll come back to that.

caption: Refused: orders are accepted only for clients with approved KYC
vo: And there's the answer. No approved KYC, no order. The rule runs on the server, so nobody can skip it.

caption: Switch to Natacha Hardy — KYC approved, conservative profile
vo: So let's switch to Natacha Hardy. Her KYC is approved, but she's conservative. Her profile allows products up to risk one, and this bond fund is rated two.

caption: Refused again: the fund is riskier than her profile
vo: Refused again, because the fund is riskier than her profile. To go ahead, Vanessa records why Natacha still wants it, and that she's acknowledged the higher risk.

caption: With the override documented, capture the order
vo: Override documented. Now she captures the order as the maker.

caption: Order captured — an operations checker will authorise it
vo: The order starts at Captured. Next, an operations checker has to authorise it.

caption: On the pipeline, move the order to Checks complete
vo: On the pipeline, Vanessa moves it to Checks complete. That's the hand-off to Operations.

caption: Blocked: the payment proof must be received first
vo: Blocked. Remember that payment proof? No order reaches Operations without it.

caption: The client's transfer has arrived — tick "Payment proof received"
vo: A little later, Natacha's transfer arrives. So Vanessa edits the order and ticks payment proof received.

caption: Move it again
vo: Now the gate opens, and an approval is raised.

caption: An approval request goes to the operations checkers
vo: It goes to the operations checkers. That's maker-checker: whoever captured the order can never approve it.

caption: Vanessa has nothing to approve here
vo: So Vanessa's approvals are empty. Her own order went to Operations.

caption: The operations checker reviews and approves
vo: Let's go to the checker.

caption: Sign in as Ritesh Seewoo — Operations Checker
vo: This is Ritesh Seewoo, the operations checker who authorises fund orders.

caption: He opens the order first: payment proof, amount, suitability override
vo: Before approving anything, Ritesh opens the order. He checks the payment proof, the amount, and the suitability override with Natacha's reasons. He sees everything Vanessa recorded, but he can't change any of it. That's the point of a checker.

caption: Approved — the system does the rest
vo: He approves, and the system takes it from there. It sends the order to the transfer agent, records the reference, confirms, emails the client and books the units.

caption: Back with the fund manager: the order is Confirmed
vo: Sent to the TA, then Confirmed, and nobody typed a thing.

caption: Sign in as Vanessa Ah-Kee — Fund Manager
vo: Back to Vanessa, to check the outcome.

caption: The transfer agent's reference is on the order: TA-6175483
vo: The transfer agent's reference is right there on the order. And the units allotted are worked out at the latest NAV.

caption: The client was emailed a confirmation
vo: Natacha got her confirmation by email, in her own language.

caption: The audit trail: who captured, who approved, every stage change
vo: And the audit trail shows who captured, who approved, and every stage change. Always two different people.

caption: Fund Holdings: her new FMB 2029 units
vo: Here are Natacha's new Fixed Maturity Bond 2029 units. Units times the latest NAV gives the value, with the gain against book cost alongside.

caption: Fund Campaigns: the FMB 2029 series
vo: This fund is sold in series. Each one goes from Planned, to Window open, Allocating, and Closed.

caption: Series 2 is open: target, amount subscribed and progress
vo: Series 2 is open right now. Every linked subscription counts toward the target, converted to rupees.

caption: The Investment Funds dashboard
vo: And the Investment Funds dashboard pulls it together. Holdings value, investors, orders waiting on the transfer agent, and how the campaign is raising.

caption: Subscriptions vs redemptions, orders by fund and per month
vo: Subscriptions against redemptions, orders by fund and by month. Each one opens the records behind it.

caption: A fund subscription, end to end
vo: So that's a fund subscription, end to end. KYC and suitability checked, payment proven, maker and checker kept apart, and the transfer agent handled automatically.
